strings.name: Thierry Henry
strings.summary: Thierry Henry became an emblematic Arsenal striker through his pace, movement and curling finishes. He won the World Cup and European Championship with France and a treble with Barcelona. After retiring, he worked in coaching and broadcasting, leading France to Olympic silver in Paris. In 2026 he became sportswear brand On’s Director of Football, helping develop its football business.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: A World Cup winner and emblematic Arsenal goalscorer with lasting influence on English and French football.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Arsenal’s attacking standard
strings.highlights.h1.text: Scored 228 goals for Arsenal, won four Premier League Golden Boots and helped the club complete its unbeaten 2003–04 league campaign.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Developed in the Paris area and trained through Clairefontaine and Monaco’s youth system.
strings.highlights.h2.title: International and European honours
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won the 1998 World Cup and Euro 2000 with France and Barcelona’s league, cup and Champions League treble in 2009.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Football management at On
strings.timeline.t1.text: On announced Henry as Director of Football after preparatory work since late 2025, covering products, player partnerships and football culture.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Olympic silver and departure
strings.timeline.t2.text: Coached France to the Paris men’s Olympic silver medal and left the French youth and Olympic coaching position in August.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Retired as a player
strings.timeline.t3.text: Announced his retirement after finishing his professional playing career with the New York Red Bulls, then pursued broadcasting and coaching.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Barcelona treble
strings.timeline.t4.text: Contributed in attack as Barcelona won La Liga, the Copa del Rey and Champions League, extending his club achievements beyond England.
strings.timeline.t5.title: An unbeaten league season
strings.timeline.t5.text: Helped Arsenal win the 2003–04 Premier League without a league defeat and took the season’s Golden Boot.
strings.timeline.t6.title: European champion
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the European Championship with France as an attacker in successive major international triumphs.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Arsenal
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moved from Juventus to Arsenal and developed from a wide player into a prolific striker under Arsène Wenger.
strings.timeline.t8.title: World Cup winner
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the World Cup on home soil as a young France international.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Professional start at Monaco
strings.timeline.t9.text: Progressed through youth development into Monaco’s first team and began his professional career.
